paragraph: When did life **originate** on Earth? Where did such rumors **originate**? We must find out where this fire **originates**.
english: to begin or come from

paragraph: Do you have a **receipt**? This is just to confirm **receipt** of your letter. Here is the **receipt**. Remember to bring everything along.
english: the act of receiving, or the fact of having been received

paragraph: The **matrix** consisted of five rows and seven columns. Do you remember the agents in the **Matrix**? We live in a media **matrix**.
english: the cavity or mold in which anything is formed

paragraph: The living room is **adjacent** to the dining room. Check this room while I check the **adjacent** one. The post office is **adjacent** to the library.
english: lying next to, close, or contiguous

paragraph: I wanted to show them my **appreciation**. You show your **appreciation** to them through the poetry. Show **appreciation** for the beauty of art and culture.
english: a just valuation or estimate of merit, worth, weight, etc.; recognition of excellence

paragraph: Our **athletic** meet took place only three days ago. The **athletic** meet was put off until next week. **Athletic** boys are popular with girls in American schools.
english: physically strong and active; relating to sports

paragraph: The **cruelest** lies are often told in silence. It would be very **cruel** to neglect the elderly. It was **cruel** of him to beat his dog.
english: that intentionally causes pain and suffering
arabicDesc: مثال: اقسى انواع الكذب هو غالباً ما يقال في صمت.

paragraph: I've just seen the first **deer** since the snow. Our hunting dog took off after a big **deer**. The **deer** was sleeping on a bed of leaves.
english: the meat of such an animal, obtained through the process of hunting or from specialized deer farms

paragraph: The store around the corner sells **Delta**-8.
english: the fourth letter of the modern Greek alphabet Δ, δ

paragraph: The **Electoral** College is a disaster for a democracy. By a hair he wasn't excluded from the **electoral** race. The **electoral** law needs to be changed.
english: relating to elections

paragraph: Since 1990, **eleven** female students received the award. I usually start work at **eleven** in the morning. I waited for you in the park until **eleven**.
english: the cardinal number occurring after ten and before twelve
arabicDesc: مثال: منذ ١٩٩۰م و حتّى الآن ، استلمت الجائزة إحدى عشرة طالبةً.

paragraph: Don't bother with **excessive** details. You don't need them now. **Excessive** supply leads to a drop in prices. The enemy of true freedom is an **excessive** call for security.
english: exceeding the usual bounds of something

paragraph: They're done with stealing computers. They're stealing **jewelry** now. I want to report the loss of some **jewelry**. What kind of **jewelry** do you like to wear?
english: rings, necklaces and other things worn for decoration

paragraph: **Journalism** is the first rough draft of history. **Journalism** should at least be a little biased. Why did you decide on majoring in **journalism**?
english: the work of collecting and reporting news

paragraph: This system of **linear** equations has exactly one solution.
english: in a straight line; step by step

paragraph: He doesn't travel much apart from **occasional** business trips. Other than **occasional** business trips, I don't travel much. Man is a predator with **occasional** human methods.
english: occurring or appearing irregularly from time to time, but not often

paragraph: I have a very **unfortunate** announcement to make today. It's **unfortunate** that you have already booked your ticket. It would be **unfortunate** if he were to fail.
english: unlucky; regrettable

paragraph: Unfortunately, it was impossible for us to **notify** you. If you don't come tomorrow, **notify** me by phone. I will **notify** you of the result in one week.
english: to give (someone) notice (of some event)

paragraph: He broke his **jaw** and lost a few teeth. Since the tooth is broken, how could the **jaw** work? When I heard about it, my **jaw** dropped.
english: one of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth

paragraph: Who has been using my **towel**? He can use this **towel** again. What is this **towel** made of?
english: cloth used for wiping

paragraph: The dog was trying to get the **collar** off. The **collar** broke off and the dog ran away. It's the same dog with a different **collar**.
english: clothes that encircle the neck

other.meaning: fabric garment part fitting around throat

paragraph: People started using that **cemetery** again. We are going to the **cemetery**. Let's go through the **cemetery**. It's closer that way.
english: a place where dead people are buried
arabicDesc: مثال: بدأ الناس يستعملون تلك المقبرة مجددا.

paragraph: The tax base determines the **calculation** of the tax. Have you allowed for any error in your **calculation**? There are a lot of results and a **calculation** mistakes.
english: the act or process of calculating

paragraph: I'm a detective, not an **economist**. His father is a famous **economist**. This **economist** studies the global economy.
english: an expert in economics, especially one who studies economic data and extracts higher-level information or proposes theories

paragraph: Enthusiasm is gradually giving way to doubt and **uncertainty**. All forecasts have a certain degree of **uncertainty**. We're living in a time of great **uncertainty**.
english: not being sure

paragraph: I ran **setup** and then the whole thing crashed. The whole thing was a **setup**. It feels like a **setup**.
english: the way something is organized

paragraph: I prefer taking medicine rather than getting an **injection**. The nurse administered an **injection** to the patient. All that's required is one **injection** and some electronic devices.
english: the act of injecting, or something that is injected

paragraph: The **applicant** didn't know how to answer the question. The job **applicant** did not meet the expectations of the employer. Does the **applicant** have suitable abilities to carry out the job?
english: one who applies for something

paragraph: We need to connect this cable to the **generator**. Many games use dice as a random number **generator**. The power is out, but we have a **generator**.
english: one who, or that which, generates, begets, causes, or produces

paragraph: The **prosecutor** asked me a leading question. He submitted the evidence to the **prosecutor**. A new **prosecutor** took over the case from the previous one.
english: a prosecuting attorney

paragraph: Hold on. I need to get my **broker** on the phone. My insurance **broker** sells both home and vehicle insurance but not life insurance. So, **brokers**, what do you want to give me?
english: a mediator between a buyer and seller

paragraph: This **berry** is good to eat. She arranged fresh **berries** on top of the cake. They served us **berries** and fresh fruit for breakfast.
english: a small succulent fruit, of any one of many varieties

paragraph: The wood **troll** lived deep in the woods. I run a fake numbers station just to **troll** people. That man sure knows how to **troll**.
english: a giant supernatural being, especially a grotesque humanoid creature living in caves or hills or under bridges

paragraph: The **gem** I bought from the shop is authentic. She stumbled upon a hidden **gem** of a book. She was a real **gem** of a person.
english: a precious stone, usually of substantial monetary value or prized for its beauty or shine

paragraph: How long does it usually take to **rotate** tires? When you turn this handle, the gears **rotate**. **Rotate** your screen to see other images.
english: to spin, turn, or revolve

paragraph: Always treat a **firearm** as if it's loaded. He accidentally discharged his **firearm**. A lion took his **firearm**.
english: a personal weapon that uses explosive powder to propel a projectile often made of lead

paragraph: What are you doing, **darling**? Believe me, **darling**, the stars were made for falling. I beg you, my **darling**... Please don't leave me.
english: often used as an affectionate term of address: a person who is very dear to one

paragraph: A **prophet** is not recognized in his own land. Never was a **prophet** valued in his native country. He bought a book about the **prophet** of Islam.
english: someone who speaks by divine inspiration

paragraph: You have a **tendency** to cover up your anxieties. That has been the **tendency** for the last 20 years. You have an annoying **tendency** of interrupting me.
english: a likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction

paragraph: I feel completely **refreshed** after spending a week in the country. I get an error when I **refresh** the page. She looked at the picture to **refresh** her memory.
english: to renew or revitalize
arabicDesc: مثال: أشعر بانتعاش تام بعد أن قضيت أسبوعا في البلاد.

paragraph: I try to see the **lighter** side of things. We're going to need a new **lighter** real soon. Is it a bit **lighter** or a bit heavier?
english: a person who lights (“sets fire to or ignites”) a thing

paragraph: Each **molecule** in our body has a unique shape. A **molecule** is made up of atoms. An atom is smaller than a **molecule**.
english: the smallest particle of a specific element or compound that retains the chemical properties of that element or compound

paragraph: I thought I told you to **trim** your beard. Some people stay **trim** even without going to a gym. I need to **trim** my nails since they're too long.
english: to reduce slightly

paragraph: The main **shareholder** requested an extraordinary meeting. **Shareholders** with questions, please raise your hands. The **shareholders** meeting was held.
english: one who owns shares of stock in a corporation

paragraph: She's in **consultation** with the doctor right now. I had a **consultation** with a lawyer about my will. With these words, she ended the **consultation**.
english: the act of consulting

paragraph: The taste is fine, but the **texture** is awful. Black-eyed beans add **texture** to dishes. Line art emphasizes form and outline, over color, shading, and **texture**.
english: the feel or shape of a surface or substance

paragraph: In American football, a **touchdown** scores six points. A **touchdown** is worth 6 points. Tom scored the game-winning **touchdown**.
english: when a plane lands; a score in American football
arabic: هبوط / هدف في كرة القدم الأمريكية

paragraph: **Preach** what you do, and do what you **preach**. A full stomach likes to **preach** about fasting. Stop smoking, doctor, and practice what you **preach**.
english: to give a sermon

paragraph: I plan to major in **cognitive** science in college. Do you believe language learning can enhance **cognitive** abilities? Why? I'm majoring in **cognitive** science in college.
english: relating to the part of mental functions that deals with logic, as opposed to affective which deals with emotions

paragraph: The doctor will have to check their **dental** records. How do I complain about my **dental** treatment? The **dental** program is visiting the village tonight.
english: of or concerning the teeth

paragraph: That country broke off **diplomatic** relations with the United States. The two countries expressed interest in establishing **diplomatic** ties. The two countries have had no **diplomatic** ties since 1979.
english: concerning relationships between governments
arabicDesc: مثال: قطع ذلك البلد العلاقات الدبلوماسية مع الولايات المتحدة.

paragraph: That every one who believes in him may have **eternal** life. The **eternal** silence of these infinite spaces terrifies me. All loves are **eternal**. What changes is the person.
english: lasting forever
arabicDesc: مثال: لكي لا يهلك كل من يؤمن به بل تكون له الحياة الأبدية.

paragraph: She purchased a **generic** version of a medication. **Generic** medications are almost always cheaper.
english: very broad

paragraph: **Grandma** went to the market to buy food for the family. **Grandma** is three and a half times your age. My **grandma** knows all the roads in the village.
english: grandmother (informal) — see also granny
arabicDesc: مثال: الجدة ذهبت الي السوق لشراء طعام للأسرة.

paragraph: Only a **handful** of people came to the meeting. I listened to a **handful** of episodes, maybe five. I will show you fear in a **handful** of dust.
english: the amount that a hand will grasp or contain

paragraph: You only have one life. Live it **happily** and successfully. And they all lived **happily** ever after. Long long ago in India, a monkey, a fox, and a rabbit lived **happily** together.
english: in a happy manner
arabicDesc: مثال: لديك حياة واحدة فقط ، فلتعشها بسعادة و نجاح.

paragraph: They only eat fruits and vegetables that are grown **locally**. These goods may not be available **locally**. All the vegetables are **locally** grown.
english: in the local area

paragraph: The risk of injury in this sport is **minimal**. I think that the economic impact will be **minimal**. Abstract art can be **minimal** or extremely elaborate.
english: very small

paragraph: This **molecular** structure is unlike anything I've ever seen. Organic compounds are generally **molecular** compounds.
english: relating to, or consisting of, or produced by molecules

paragraph: You have to get this work finished by **noon**. The constitutional court will issue a decision by **noon** today. I have lunch at **noon** with my friends.
english: the time of day when the Sun seems to reach its highest point in the sky
arabicDesc: مثال: يجب عليك أن تنهي هذا العمل قبل الظهر.

paragraph: Meat is very expensive **nowadays**. **Nowadays** anybody can get books. **Nowadays** marriage is not necessarily a must for women.
english: at the present time

paragraph: There were some **openly** gay guys at high school. I'm not going to discuss this subject **openly** with you. He's never **openly** expressed his feelings about death.
english: without hiding

paragraph: We had lost the **overview** a long time ago. I like to have an **overview** of things. We gave a quick **overview** of our findings.
english: a general description

paragraph: The education in that institute is simply **pathetic**. Look at those **pathetic** tourists on the bus. The acting in this series is **pathetic**.
english: very bad or weak; causing pity

paragraph: Above all things, we must not be **selfish**. I don't intend to be **selfish**. Why are you so **selfish**?
english: having regard for one's own well-being above that of others
arabicDesc: مثال: قبل كل شيء، يجب ألا نكون أنانيين.

paragraph: This is so annoying. I'm getting **spam** again. That one got through the **spam** filter. That was an odd bit of **spam**.
english: any undesired electronic content automatically generated for commercial purposes

paragraph: I received an email **notification** of his upcoming party. We didn't receive any **notification** of his having been fired. I received **notification** that we must move out in one month.
english: the act of notifying

other.meaning: a specific piece of information serving to notify

paragraph: I'm afraid to fall, please **prop** me up. Could you **prop** up this mirror against that wall for me? **Prop** the ladder against the wall.
english: an object placed against or under another, to support it

other.meaning: To support or shore up something (verb)

paragraph: The cake is still in the **oven**. Turn off the **oven**! I can smell something burning. You left the cookies in the **oven** too long.
english: chamber used for baking or heating
arabicDesc: مثال: ما زالت الكعكة في الفرن.

paragraph: I could also take a **placement** test, if necessary. The college has a **placement** bureau for students. My **placement** supervisor allowed me to take a day off.
english: the act of placing or putting in place

paragraph: The time spent to see the **monument** is short. There is a **monument** in front of the museum. This **monument** is more than one hundred years old.
english: a structure built for commemorative or symbolic reasons, or as a memorial

paragraph: Is there life on **Titan**? I'm living on **Titan** now. I could not persuade the **Titans**.
english: any of the race of giant gods in Greek mythology that preceded and was overthrown by the Olympian gods

paragraph: New political **obstacles** have emerged. She has the wonderful capability to overcome any **obstacle**. We'll have to face every **obstacle** that comes our way.
english: something that impedes, stands in the way of, or holds up progress, either physically or figuratively

paragraph: A **bout** lasts about five minutes. That **bout** will be looked into in the next few years. Mary wiped away her tears, fighting back a fresh **bout**.
english: a short period of illness or activity; a boxing match
arabicDesc: مثال: تستغرق النوبة حوالي خمس دقائق.

paragraph: Have you decided on the subject of your **thesis**? You should delete any unnecessary words from your **thesis**. I'm currently looking for a topic for my **thesis**.
english: senses relating to logic, rhetoric, etc

paragraph: The author revised his **manuscript** over and over again. He is writing the **manuscript** over and over again. Can you manage to complete the **manuscript** by Friday?
english: handwritten, or by extension manually typewritten, as opposed to being mechanically reproduced

other.meaning: A book, composition or any other document, written by hand (or manually typewritten), not mechanically reproduced (noun)

paragraph: When spring comes, the flowers on trees will **bloom**. In the garden, many flowers are in **bloom** now. A lot of flowers begin to **bloom** in spring.
english: to produce flowers

paragraph: With this **module** you can make the Enter key generate an event. It's an international relations **module**.
english: a self-contained component of a system, often interchangeable, which has a well-defined interface to the other components

paragraph: The towel **rack** is fixed. This is exactly where I want the towel **rack**. Where do you want to put the towel **rack**?
english: frame for hanging objects

paragraph: His extensive knowledge of music was a **revelation** to us. Music is a higher **revelation** than all wisdom and philosophy. It's not a particularly brilliant **revelation** of mine.
english: the act of revealing or disclosing

other.meaning: The final book of the New Testament of the Bible (noun)

paragraph: Teach me how to play a **reed** pipe. There are **reed** beds on the far shore. The **reed** bends in the wind.
english: any of various types of tall stiff perennial grass-like plants growing together in groups near water

paragraph: Does only a man **inherit** what the parents left? The prince, or the princess, will **inherit** the throne. He didn't **inherit** anything from what his father left.
english: to receive property or a title by legal succession etc.

paragraph: When he heard the news, he turned **pale**. The very thought of snakes makes her turn **pale**. Your face just turned **pale** all of a sudden.
english: light in color
arabicDesc: مثال: عندما سَمِعَ الأخبار, تحولَ شاحباً.

paragraph: The crisis could start a revolution in economic **ideology**. But it was not, in fact, the end of **ideology**. They're enforcing their gender **ideology** on our children.
english: doctrine, philosophy, body of beliefs or principles belonging to an individual or group

paragraph: I like to take things apart to see what makes them **tick**. There were hundreds of **ticks** in its fur. The only sound to be heard was the **ticking** of the clock.
english: a tiny woodland arachnid of the suborder Ixodida
arabicDesc: مثال: أحب تفكيك الاشياء لمعرفة كيفية عملها.

paragraph: Are you going to **terminate** my contract? I want to **terminate** my lease. She decided to **terminate** her pregnancy.
english: to end

paragraph: Could you please **clarify** a few things for me? He did not **clarify** when it had happened. Do you need me to **clarify** anything further?
english: to make or become clear or bright by freeing from impurities or turbidity

paragraph: The man caught the girl by the **wrist**. I broke my **wrist** when I fell on it. She got away with a slap on the **wrist**.
english: joint where the hand is attached to the arm
arabicDesc: مثال: أمسك الرجلُ الفتاةَ من معصمها.

paragraph: Sugar **dissolves** in warm coffee. **Dissolve** the powder in a bucket of warm water. Sugar will **dissolve** quickly in a glass of water.
english: to mix into a liquid; to end officially
arabicDesc: مثال: يذوب السكر في القهوة الدافئة.

paragraph: I am going to **assert** his guilt. He knows how to **assert** himself. I know how to **assert** myself.
english: to state firmly

paragraph: You can only buy the medicine with a **prescription**. I don't want to be on any **prescription** medicine. Let me write you a **prescription** for some medicine.
english: the medicine or treatment provided by such an order

other.meaning: extinctive or liberative prescription — see also statute of limitations

paragraph: He was appointed **adviser** to the board. Mr Brown is our financial **adviser**. Fear is not a good **adviser**.
english: a person who gives advice

paragraph: My laser **printer** only prints in black and white. You need to put more paper in the **printer**. My computer doesn't seem to be connecting to the **printer**.
english: one who makes prints

paragraph: Oh, woman, you are the best **wizard** in the world! The princess was captured by an evil **wizard**. An engineer is a **wizard** whose magic works.
english: someone, usually male, who uses (or has skill with) magic, mystic items, and magical and mystical practices

paragraph: Don't worry. The **ambulance** will be here soon. This clinic doesn't even have an **ambulance**. Stay put. I'm calling an **ambulance**.
english: emergency vehicle
arabicDesc: مثال: لا تقلق. سيارة الإسعاف ستكون هنا قريباً.

paragraph: There are four ways to **amend** the Constitution. Some people want to **amend** the constitution. We'll need to **amend** the contract so that we can pay you more.
english: to make better

paragraph: The **duo** will split the $63,000 prize. **Duo**, the owl, teaches many languages. The **duo** arrived on stage.
english: two people working together

paragraph: Use a **marker** on the case label, not the disc. That's a **marker**, not a pen. Can permanent **marker** stains be removed?
english: a thick pen; a sign

paragraph: Did you give a copy of the **disk** to anyone? What size hard **disk** would you recommend that I buy? It looks like your hard **disk** is fragmented.
english: a thin, flat, circular plate
arabicDesc: مثال: هل أعطيت نسخة من القرص لأي شخص؟

paragraph: How do you find the volume of a **cylinder**? The **cylinder** head of the car is broken. My car has a four-**cylinder** engine.
english: a surface created by projecting a closed two-dimensional curve along an axis intersecting the plane of the curve
